scenes.title: VPC longest-prefix route selection
scenes.visual_overview: This original slide illustrates vpc longest-prefix route selection with AWS network topology and explicit route examples.
visual_walkthrough: Identify VPC and subnet or gateway boundaries

Start at the left route table: ten dot zero slash sixteen routes locally, the more specific ten dot zero dot twelve slash twenty-four route targets a Transit Gateway, and zero slash zero targets a NAT Gateway. On the right, destination ten dot zero dot twelve dot forty-two matches all three entries, so the slash twenty-four wins. A public destination such as eight dot eight dot eight dot eight matches only the default route, so it goes to NAT. The local route is not automatically preferred over a more specific supported route. The lower cards add that subnet route table association, return routing and security rules also determine end-to-end success.

scenes.narration: This slide teaches vpc longest-prefix route selection by following the pictured VPC architecture. Start at the left route table: ten dot zero slash sixteen routes locally, the more specific ten dot zero dot twelve slash twenty-four route targets a Transit Gateway, and zero slash zero targets a NAT Gateway. On the right, destination ten dot zero dot twelve dot forty-two matches all three entries, so the slash twenty-four wins. A public destination such as eight dot eight dot eight dot eight matches only the default route, so it goes to NAT. The local route is not automatically preferred over a more specific supported route. The lower cards add that subnet route table association, return routing and security rules also determine end-to-end success. Choose the longest matching prefix and check return route and security filtering. For a professional architecture decision, inspect the source and destination addresses, the effective route table associated with the subnet, and the security boundaries. A correct route without the right policy or a return path does not prove end-to-end connectivity. Treat the concrete values in the diagram as a worked example of this decision, not as a configuration that every workload must reuse.

scenes.title: Route-selection practice with local and remote destinations
scenes.visual_overview: This original slide illustrates route-selection practice with local and remote destinations with AWS network topology and explicit route examples.
visual_walkthrough: Identify VPC and subnet or gateway boundaries

This second example reinforces the earlier slide with additional destinations rather than a different routing rule. The left table includes a Transit Gateway route for ten dot forty dot twelve slash twenty-four, a broader ten dot forty slash sixteen route, the VPC local ten dot zero slash sixteen route and a zero slash zero default route through NAT. The right-hand practice questions compare destination ten dot forty dot twelve dot forty-two, which selects the most specific Transit Gateway slash twenty-four; destination ten dot zero dot five dot eight, which selects local slash sixteen; and destination eight dot eight dot eight dot eight, which uses the NAT default route. If static and propagated entries share the same prefix, review documented route-priority behavior.
